text:
chris: Heads up — eu-west-1 ALB started serving the wrong certs to some model-serving ingresses after the cert rotation at ~03:12 UTC. Readiness checks failing -> GPUs are sitting idle. Anyone else seeing this?

maya: Seeing it. ELB/ALB logs show TLS handshake failures and 502s. Health checks are flapping. Sample ALB access log: 
```
https 2026-03-17T03:14:12.123Z app/abcd1234 10.0.5.12:443 10.0.7.18:8080 0.000 0.005 502 502 0 123 "GET /healthz HTTP/1.1" "ELB-HealthChecker/2.0" TLS-Handshake-Failed SNI: -
```

samir: Sounds like an SNI mismatch. If the client doesn't send SNI ALB falls back to the default cert. That would give an unexpected cert to model-serving.x.redwood.ai.

chris: We rotated the wildcard cert (redwood-prod-2026) and applied via cert-manager + alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/certificate-arn on most ingresses. But ALB listener still has the old default cert attached in some cases. Could be listener/certs ordering or clients missing SNI.

emily: Important detail: many model-serving requests originate from our Dedicated runtime via internal egress + Envoy chain. We sometimes terminate/reencrypt TLS and that can remove SNI. If Envoy/TCP passthrough is misconfigured clients may not present SNI to ALB.

ingress-bot: Event: Namespace model-serving - Warning FailingELBHealthCheck 6m (x5 over 6m) - pods failed ELB health check: HTTP 502
```
Name:               model-serving
Namespace:          model-serving
Annotations:
  alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/certificate-arn: arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:123456789012:certificate/redwood-prod-2026
  alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/listen-ports: [{"HTTPS":443}]
Events:
  Type    Reason                    Age   From          Message
  ----    ------                    ----  ----          -------
  Warning FailingELBHealthCheck    6m    ingress/alb  Pod "ms-abc-123" failed ELB health check (502)
```

chris: Quick grab from AWS side — describe-listeners shows 2 cert ARNs attached but default listener is still the old app cert in some AZs. Output snippet: 
```
Listeners:
- Port: 443
  ListenerArn: arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:...:listener/app/.../abcd
  Certificates:
    - CertificateArn: arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:123456789012:certificate/redwood-old
    - CertificateArn: arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:123456789012:certificate/redwood-prod-2026
  DefaultActions: [ ... ]
```

maya: Running `aws elbv2 describe-listener-certificates --listener-arn ...` shows the new cert attached but ALB still returns default under certain connections. I can reproduce by curling the ALB IP without SNI: `openssl s_client -connect alb-eu:443 -no_tls1_3` -> returns old cert.

samir: That matches. Some clients (non-SNI or internal IP routed) will get default cert. For mTLS, ALB doesn't do client-cert verification upstream; we rely on Envoy for mTLS. If Envoy got a rotated cert only on its side but ALB serves old cert at TCP handshake time, the TLS handshake can fail.

emily: Short-term mitigation options:
- Attach host-specific cert via per-ingress annotation so the ALB can match by SNI for that hostname.
- Create a dedicated ALB for model-serving (so certs/listeners isolated).
- If we need real mTLS passthrough, switch that traffic to an NLB/TCP passthrough + Envoy handling TLS.

chris: Canary plan: create a dedicated ALB in eu-west-1 for model-serving only, attach the new cert as default, move 10% of traffic. That avoids fiddling with listener priority across many host rules. Can someone spin up a canary ingress with a dedicated LB name?

maya: I'll create a canary ingress with its own load balancer name and cert. Draft ingress YAML I'm about to apply: 
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: modellb-canary
  namespace: modellb-canary
  annotations:
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme: internet-facing
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/load-balancer-name: modellb-eu1-canary
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/certificate-arn: arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:123456789012:certificate/redwood-prod-2026
spec:
  rules:
    - host: model-serving-canary.x.redwood.ai
      http:
        paths:
        - backend: { service: model-svc, port: { number: 8080 } }
          path: /
```

samir: Also: temporarily bump the ASG min for GPU nodes in eu-west-1 to avoid the autoscaler terminating pods during this flapping. Right now pods failing readiness -> scale-down -> capacity waste. I'll set min=6 for the cluster.

deploy-bot: deploy modellb-canary v2026.03.17-rc2 -> eu-west-1 :white_check_mark:

chris: Thanks. Maya please open an AWS support ticket if ALB keeps choosing the old cert despite the new cert being attached. Also add a short-term Prometheus alert for ALB TLS handshake failure rate > 50/min and an oncall runbook entry pointing to this thread.

maya: On it. Opening AWS ticket now (ticket 987654321) and pushing the canary. I'll post any updates here and the final rollback steps if we see issues.
